fallacies.name: A priori argument
fallacies.summary: Selecting reasons only to defend a predetermined conclusion while insulating it from contrary evidence.
fallacies.body: Selecting reasons only to defend a predetermined conclusion while insulating it from contrary evidence. In some rhetoric catalogs this label describes dogmatic rationalization, rather than legitimate reasoning independent of experience. The defect is treating the conclusion as immune to the evidence that is supposedly being assessed. The diagnostic question is whether the stated support raises the probability or credibility of the conclusion independently of the conclusion itself. Identify the missing bridge, test its reliability, and distinguish an unsupported premise from a premise that is merely controversial. A sound repair supplies that bridge or narrows the claim. In this case, inspect the move from the stated support to the conclusion rather than judging the speaker’s confidence. The example I already know this treatment always works, so any failed trial must have been designed incorrectly. is diagnostic only if that inferential move is present.

examples.text: I already know this treatment always works, so any failed trial must have been designed incorrectly.

fallacies.detectionCriteria: Flag the pattern only when the argument A conclusion is held fixed, and every contrary result is dismissed without an independently supported reason and the stated support does not independently establish the conclusion.
doesNotCountWhen: A priori reasoning in mathematics or philosophy is not fallacious merely because it does not begin with an experiment. The relevant form must be present in the actual argument, not inferred from a shared topic.

fallacies.name: Abusive ad hominem
fallacies.summary: The argument rejects a claim by attacking its proponent's character instead of addressing the claim.
fallacies.body: The argument rejects a claim by attacking its proponent's character instead of addressing the claim. A person's faults do not by themselves make the person's proposition false. Separate the conclusion’s truth conditions from the social force of the speaker, audience, emotion, or consequence. Ask what evidence would remain if the appeal were removed. An appeal can be rhetorically effective or morally relevant in another context while still failing to establish this proposition. In this case, inspect the move from the stated support to the conclusion rather than judging the speaker’s confidence. The example Lena says the bridge design fails a load test, but Lena is dishonest, so the design is safe. is diagnostic only if that inferential move is present.

examples.text: Lena says the bridge design fails a load test, but Lena is dishonest, so the design is safe.

fallacies.detectionCriteria: Flag the pattern only when the argument The response targets the speaker's character while leaving the stated evidence unanswered and the stated support does not independently establish the conclusion.
doesNotCountWhen: Relevant evidence about a speaker's reliability counts when it directly bears on testimony or motive and is not treated as a refutation by itself. The relevant form must be present in the actual argument, not inferred from a shared topic.

fallacies.name: Accent fallacy
fallacies.summary: The argument changes a sentence's meaning by shifting emphasis or stress between words.
fallacies.body: The argument changes a sentence's meaning by shifting emphasis or stress between words. Spoken emphasis can create a different proposition from the one actually asserted or written without that emphasis. Mark the exact word, scope, accent, or grammatical attachment that changes between premises and conclusion. Restate the argument with one stable meaning for each term, then test whether the inference survives. If clarification removes the problem, the original exchange was unclear rather than refuted. In this case, inspect the move from the stated support to the conclusion rather than judging the speaker’s confidence. The example The contract says the tenant must pay rent on time, and the landlord stresses must to claim that late payment is never excusable under any circumstance. is diagnostic only if that inferential move is present.

examples.text: The contract says the tenant must pay rent on time, and the landlord stresses must to claim that late payment is never excusable under any circumstance.

fallacies.detectionCriteria: Flag the pattern only when the argument A disputed conclusion depends on an unmarked or misleading change in word stress or typographical emphasis and the stated support does not independently establish the conclusion.
doesNotCountWhen: Clarifying intended emphasis or distinguishing genuinely different readings is not fallacious. The relevant form must be present in the actual argument, not inferred from a shared topic.

fallacies.name: Accident
fallacies.summary: The argument applies a general rule to an exceptional case where its usual conditions do not hold.
fallacies.body: The argument applies a general rule to an exceptional case where its usual conditions do not hold. A rule framed for ordinary cases can mislead when a special circumstance defeats its purpose or scope. Inspect the route from the observed cases to the broader population: who was included, who was missing, and which outcome was measured. Ask whether the sample differs on a feature that could change the result. A narrow claim supported by a representative sample is not the same error as a universal claim drawn from anecdotes. In this case, inspect the move from the stated support to the conclusion rather than judging the speaker’s confidence. The example One should return borrowed property, so a doctor must return a delirious patient's loaded pistol immediately. is diagnostic only if that inferential move is present.

examples.text: One should return borrowed property, so a doctor must return a delirious patient's loaded pistol immediately.

fallacies.detectionCriteria: Flag the pattern only when the argument A universal or broad rule is applied without accounting for a relevant exception recognized by the rule's purpose and the stated support does not independently establish the conclusion.
doesNotCountWhen: Applying a rule to a case that satisfies its stated conditions and lacks a relevant exception is legitimate. The relevant form must be present in the actual argument, not inferred from a shared topic.

fallacies.name: Ad fidentia

fallacies.name: Ad hoc rescue
fallacies.summary: The argument adds an unsupported special assumption solely to protect a claim from a counterexample.

fallacies.name: Affirmative conclusion from a negative premise
fallacies.summary: The syllogistic inference draws an affirmative conclusion from at least one negative premise.
fallacies.body: The syllogistic inference draws an affirmative conclusion from at least one negative premise. In standard categorical syllogisms a negative premise requires a negative conclusion because it denies a predicate relation. Check the inference by translating its relevant form, preserving the intended quantifier scope and connective. If a valuation or countermodel makes the premises true and the conclusion false, the inference fails even if the conclusion happens to be true. Validity and truth of the particular conclusion must be kept separate. In this case, inspect the move from the stated support to the conclusion rather than judging the speaker’s confidence. fallacies.summary: The argument uses unexplained acronyms or technical abbreviations to create an appearance of expertise in place of reasons.
fallacies.body: The argument uses unexplained acronyms or technical abbreviations to create an appearance of expertise in place of reasons. fallacies.name: Alternative truth
fallacies.summary: Presenting an incompatible factual assertion as an equally valid truth without resolving the evidential conflict.

fallacies.name: Ambiguity fallacy
fallacies.summary: The argument treats a word or phrase with multiple meanings as though it had one meaning throughout.

An equivocation changes the proposition being supported while preserving the same wording. Mark the exact word, scope, accent, or grammatical attachment that changes between premises and conclusion. fallacies.summary: It asserts what would have happened under a different condition without evidence or a justified causal model.
fallacies.body: It asserts what would have happened under a different condition without evidence or a justified causal model. An unobserved alternative outcome cannot be known merely by imagining it. Reconstruct the proposed causal path and list plausible common causes, selection effects, reverse direction, and coincidence. A temporal sequence or correlation alone does not settle which path operates. The argument becomes stronger when an intervention, comparison group, mechanism, or prediction discriminates among the live explanations. In this case, inspect the move from the stated support to the conclusion rather than judging the speaker’s confidence. The example If the city had rejected the tram, traffic would certainly have fallen because drivers would have adapted. is diagnostic only if that inferential move is present.

examples.text: If the city had rejected the tram, traffic would certainly have fallen because drivers would have adapted.

fallacies.detectionCriteria: Flag the pattern only when the argument A claim about an unobserved alternative is stated with confidence but lacks a model, comparison, or relevant evidence and the stated support does not independently establish the conclusion.
doesNotCountWhen: A credible causal design, historical comparison, or well-supported model identifies the counterfactual and uncertainty. The relevant form must be present in the actual argument, not inferred from a shared topic.

fallacies.name: Unwarranted contrast
fallacies.summary: It infers a meaningful contrast between two cases from their juxtaposition without establishing that the contrast exists.
fallacies.body: It infers a meaningful contrast between two cases from their juxtaposition without establishing that the contrast exists. Different descriptions or circumstances do not by themselves imply a causal, normative, or statistical difference. The diagnostic question is whether the stated support raises the probability or credibility of the conclusion independently of the conclusion itself. Identify the missing bridge, test its reliability, and distinguish an unsupported premise from a premise that is merely controversial. A sound repair supplies that bridge or narrows the claim. In this case, inspect the move from the stated support to the conclusion rather than judging the speaker’s confidence. The example The report says rural patients improved while urban patients improved after treatment, so the treatment works only in rural areas. is diagnostic only if that inferential move is present.

examples.text: The report says rural patients improved while urban patients improved after treatment, so the treatment works only in rural areas.

fallacies.detectionCriteria: Flag the pattern only when the argument The argument treats parallel wording or a named difference as evidence for a substantive difference without comparison data and the stated support does not independently establish the conclusion.
doesNotCountWhen: The contrast is defined in advance and supported by appropriate measurements, controls, or relevant premises. The relevant form must be present in the actual argument, not inferred from a shared topic.

fallacies.name: Use–mention error
fallacies.summary: It confuses an expression with the thing or concept that the expression denotes.
fallacies.body: It confuses an expression with the thing or concept that the expression denotes. Words, names, and quoted symbols are not identical to their referents. Mark the exact word, scope, accent, or grammatical attachment that changes between premises and conclusion. Restate the argument with one stable meaning for each term, then test whether the inference survives. If clarification removes the problem, the original exchange was unclear rather than refuted. In this case, inspect the move from the stated support to the conclusion rather than judging the speaker’s confidence. The example The name "Venus" has five letters, so the planet Venus has five letters. is diagnostic only if that inferential move is present.

examples.text: The name "Venus" has five letters, so the planet Venus has five letters.

fallacies.detectionCriteria: Flag the pattern only when the argument A predicate true of the written or spoken expression is transferred to the object named by that expression, or vice versa and the stated support does not independently establish the conclusion.
doesNotCountWhen: Quotation and reference are explicitly distinguished, so the predicate's target is clear. The relevant form must be present in the actual argument, not inferred from a shared topic.

fallacies.name: We-have-to-do-something fallacy
fallacies.summary: Inferring that a particular action is justified merely because some action is needed.
fallacies.body: Inferring that a particular action is justified merely because some action is needed. Urgency establishes a reason to seek an effective response, not a reason to accept the first available intervention. The proposed action still needs a connection to the problem and an assessment of likely consequences. The diagnostic question is whether the stated support raises the probability or credibility of the conclusion independently of the conclusion itself. Identify the missing bridge, test its reliability, and distinguish an unsupported premise from a premise that is merely controversial. A sound repair supplies that bridge or narrows the claim. In this case, inspect the move from the stated support to the conclusion rather than judging the speaker’s confidence. The example We must reduce accidents. This publicity campaign is something we can do. Therefore it will solve the accident problem. is diagnostic only if that inferential move is present.

examples.text: We must reduce accidents. This publicity campaign is something we can do. Therefore it will solve the accident problem.

fallacies.detectionCriteria: Flag the pattern only when the argument A need for action and the availability of an action are used to justify that action without the missing effectiveness premise and the stated support does not independently establish the conclusion.
doesNotCountWhen: An urgent intervention can be justified by the best available evidence despite uncertainty and limited time. The relevant form must be present in the actual argument, not inferred from a shared topic.

fallacies.name: Weak man
fallacies.summary: It refutes an opponent's position by replacing it with a less defensible version that may retain only a vague resemblance.
fallacies.body: It refutes an opponent's position by replacing it with a less defensible version that may retain only a vague resemblance. A weakened substitute does not test the actual argument and can create a false victory. Track whether the response addresses the claim under dispute or changes the conversational burden. State the strongest version of the opposing position, answer that version directly, and identify any new premise introduced by the reply. A disagreement is not a fallacy merely because the parties use different values. In this case, inspect the move from the stated support to the conclusion rather than judging the speaker’s confidence. The example A scientist says emissions should be reduced gradually, and the reply says she wants to shut down all factories tomorrow. is diagnostic only if that inferential move is present.

examples.text: A scientist says emissions should be reduced gradually, and the reply says she wants to shut down all factories tomorrow.

fallacies.detectionCriteria: Flag the pattern only when the argument The opponent's position is made more extreme, simplistic, or careless than the stated or strongest reasonable version and the stated support does not independently establish the conclusion.
doesNotCountWhen: The reconstruction preserves the original claim's scope and qualifications before criticism. The relevant form must be present in the actual argument, not inferred from a shared topic.

fallacies.name: Whataboutism
fallacies.summary: It deflects criticism by pointing to another person's alleged wrongdoing instead of addressing the criticism.
fallacies.body: It deflects criticism by pointing to another person's alleged wrongdoing instead of addressing the criticism. Another wrongdoing may be relevant to consistency or comparative policy, but it does not answer whether the original conduct was wrong. Separate the conclusion’s truth conditions from the social force of the speaker, audience, emotion, or consequence. Ask what evidence would remain if the appeal were removed. An appeal can be rhetorically effective or morally relevant in another context while still failing to establish this proposition. In this case, inspect the move from the stated support to the conclusion rather than judging the speaker’s confidence. The example Asked why our company dumped waste illegally, the manager replies that a competitor also pollutes. is diagnostic only if that inferential move is present.

fallacies.detectionCriteria: Flag the pattern only when the argument The response changes from the original allegation to a comparable allegation without resolving the original issue and the stated support does not independently establish the conclusion.
doesNotCountWhen: The comparison is directly relevant to a stated consistency, enforcement, or causal question and the original issue is also addressed. The relevant form must be present in the actual argument, not inferred from a shared topic.

fallacies.name: Wishful thinking
fallacies.summary: It treats a desired outcome as evidence that the outcome is true or will occur.
fallacies.body: It treats a desired outcome as evidence that the outcome is true or will occur. Desire can bias assessment but cannot establish facts or probabilities. Separate the conclusion’s truth conditions from the social force of the speaker, audience, emotion, or consequence. Ask what evidence would remain if the appeal were removed. An appeal can be rhetorically effective or morally relevant in another context while still failing to establish this proposition. In this case, inspect the move from the stated support to the conclusion rather than judging the speaker’s confidence. The example We want the merger to succeed, so regulators will approve it despite the missing filing. is diagnostic only if that inferential move is present.

fallacies.detectionCriteria: Flag the pattern only when the argument The conclusion is supported chiefly by hope, preference, or confidence rather than evidence about the world and the stated support does not independently establish the conclusion.
doesNotCountWhen: The desired outcome is supported by independent evidence, and optimism is explicitly treated as motivation rather than proof. The relevant form must be present in the actual argument, not inferred from a shared topic.

fallacies.name: Worst-negates-the-bad fallacy
aliases: be grateful for what you have
fallacies.summary: Dismissing a real problem solely because a worse problem exists or is imaginable.
fallacies.body: Dismissing a real problem solely because a worse problem exists or is imaginable. A comparison with a worse condition can provide perspective without refuting the original complaint. Whether the problem deserves action depends on its own severity, remedies, and opportunity costs. Track whether the response addresses the claim under dispute or changes the conversational burden. State the strongest version of the opposing position, answer that version directly, and identify any new premise introduced by the reply. A disagreement is not a fallacy merely because the parties use different values. In this case, inspect the move from the stated support to the conclusion rather than judging the speaker’s confidence. The example Your apartment has no working heat, but some people have no home, so the broken heating is not a problem. is diagnostic only if that inferential move is present.

fallacies.detectionCriteria: Flag the pattern only when the argument A problem's existence or significance is denied on the sole ground that another situation is worse and the stated support does not independently establish the conclusion.
doesNotCountWhen: Comparative severity is relevant when allocating scarce resources among competing urgent needs. The relevant form must be present in the actual argument, not inferred from a shared topic.

fallacies.name: Zero-tolerance fallacy
fallacies.summary: Assuming that eliminating every instance of a harm justifies any cost or response.
fallacies.body: Assuming that eliminating every instance of a harm justifies any cost or response. This rhetoric label concerns ignoring proportionality and alternative ways to reduce risk. A worthwhile aim does not by itself establish that unlimited expenditure or punishment is warranted. Check whether a moral, historical, or economic conclusion follows from the relevant facts and normative assumptions, rather than from a loaded description. Make the value premise explicit and examine whose costs and benefits are counted. Disagreement with the value is not by itself a logical diagnosis. In this case, inspect the move from the stated support to the conclusion rather than judging the speaker’s confidence. The example One minor reporting error is intolerable, so every employee must undergo an hour-long audit before sending any message. is diagnostic only if that inferential move is present.

examples.text: One minor reporting error is intolerable, so every employee must undergo an hour-long audit before sending any message.

fallacies.detectionCriteria: Flag the pattern only when the argument Zero occurrence is treated as overriding all other relevant costs and constraints without justification and the stated support does not independently establish the conclusion.
doesNotCountWhen: A strict rule can be justified for a narrowly defined high-severity risk when proportionate and effective. The relevant form must be present in the actual argument, not inferred from a shared topic.
